question: Wisdom lies in knowing what to reckon with and what to overlook. An officer being engrossed with the periphery ignoring the core issues before him is not rare in the Bureaucracy. Do you agree that such preoccupation of an administrator leads to travesty of justice to the cause of effective service delivery and good governance? Critically evaluate.

Apart from intellectual competency and moral qualities, empathy and compassion are some of the other vital attributes that facilitate the civil servants to be more competent in tackling crucial issues or taking critical decisions. Explain with suitable illustrations.

The Rules and Regulations provided to all the Civil servants are same, yet there is difference in the performance. Positive minded officers are able to interpret the Rules and Regulations in favour of the case and achieve success, whereas negative minded officers are unable to achieve goals by interpreting the same Rules and Regulations against the case. Discuss with illustrations.

It is believed that adherence to ethics in human actions would ensure smooth functioning of an organization/system. If so, what does ethics seek to promote in human life? How do ethical values assist in the resolution of conflicts faced by him in his day-to-day functioning?
“Ethics is knowing the difference between what you have the right to do and what is right to do.” — Potter Stewart. What does this quotation mean to you?

“If a country is to be corruption free and become a nation of beautiful minds, I strongly feel that there are three key societal members who can make a difference: father, mother and teacher.” — A. P. J. Abdul Kalam. What does this quotation mean to you?
“Judge your success by what you had to give up in order to get it.” — Dalai Lama. What does this quotation mean to you?
What do you understand by the term ‘good governance’? How far recent initiatives in terms of e-Governance steps taken by the State have helped the beneficiaries? Discuss with suitable examples.

Online methodology is being used for day-to-day meetings, institutional approvals in the administration and for teaching and learning in education sector to the extent telemedicine in the health sector is getting popular with the approval of the competent authority. No doubt it has advantages and disadvantages for both the beneficiaries and the system at large. Describe and discuss ethical issues involved in the use of the online method, particularly to the vulnerable section of the society.

Russia and Ukraine war has been going on for the last seven months. Different countries have taken independent stands and actions keeping in view their own national interests. We are all aware that war has its own impact on the different aspects of society, including human tragedy. What are those ethical issues that are crucial to be considered while launching the war and its continuation so far? Illustrate with justification the ethical issues involved in the given state of affairs.
Constitutional morality
Conflict of interest
Probity in public life
Challenges of digitalization
Devotion to duty

Whistle-blower, who reports corruption and illegal activities, wrongdoing and misconduct to the concerned authorities, runs the risk of being exposed to grave danger, physical harm and victimization by the vested interests, accused persons and his team. What policy measures would you suggest to strengthen the protection mechanism to safeguard the whistle-blower?

In the contemporary world, the corporate sector’s contribution to generating wealth and employment is increasing. In doing so, they are bringing in an unprecedented onslaught on the climate, environmental sustainability and living conditions of human beings. In this background, do you find that Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) is efficient and sufficient enough to fulfill the social roles and responsibilities needed in the corporate world for which CSR is mandated? Critically examine.

Prabhat was working as Vice President (Marketing) at Sterling Electric Ltd., a reputed multinational company. The company was passing through difficult times as sales were continuously showing a downward trend. His division was desperately trying to procure a big government order. Under pressure from the London-based Head Office, he assured management that his division was working on a special contract from the Ministry of Defence for a secret installation near Gwalior and that the tender was being submitted shortly.

A candidate, Subhash Verma, applied for a Manager position through the office of the Minister of Defence. During interview, Prabhat found him technically sound and experienced. Subhash indicated that he possessed copies of bid documents that Unique Electronics Ltd. would submit the next day to the Defence Ministry and offered to hand them over if employed on suitable terms, enabling Sterling Electric Ltd. to outbid its rival and obtain the order. Prabhat was under financial pressure due to family expenses, EMIs and his mother’s illness.

(a) Discuss the ethical issues involved in the case.
(b) Critically examine the options available to Prabhat in the above situation.
(c) Which of the above would be the most appropriate for Prabhat and why?

section: Case Study / Public Administration & Internal Security
question:
Ramesh is a State Civil Services Officer who got posted to the capital of a border State after 20 years of service. His mother has cancer and is admitted to a leading cancer hospital in the city, while his adolescent children have secured admission in good schools. As Director in the Home Department, Ramesh received intelligence about illegal migrants infiltrating the State. He conducted surprise checks and caught two families of 12 members who had infiltrated with connivance of security personnel. Investigation found forged Aadhaar, Ration and Voter cards being used to settle migrants in a particular area.

Ramesh submitted a detailed report to the Additional Secretary, but was later instructed by the Additional Home Secretary to withdraw it, with a warning that failure to do so would affect his posting and future promotion.

(a) What are the options available to Ramesh as the Director of the Home Department of the bordering State?
(b) What option should Ramesh adopt and why?
(c) Critically evaluate each of the options.
(d) What are the ethical dilemmas being faced by Ramesh?
(e) What policy measures would you suggest to combat the menace of infiltration of illegal migrants from the neighbouring country?

The Supreme Court has banned mining in the Aravalli Hills to stop degradation of forest cover and maintain ecological balance. However, stone mining continued in the border district of the affected State with connivance of corrupt forest officials and politicians. A young SP attempted to stop the menace. During a surprise check, a truck carrying stone tried to escape and the driver overran a police officer, killing him. No breakthrough was achieved for almost three months.

Ashok, an investigative journalist, investigated the case and exposed the nexus between the stone mafia, corrupt police and civil officials, and politicians. The local MLA involved was close to the Chief Minister and was also related to the owner of the TV channel. The channel CMD advised Ashok not to publish the story, offering promotion, pay hike and adjustment of a ₹10 lakh soft loan taken for his son’s chronic disease if he handed over the report.

(a) What are the options available with Ashok to cope with the situation?
(b) Critically evaluate/examine each of the options identified by Ashok.
(c) What are the ethical dilemmas being faced by Ashok?
(d) Which option would be the most appropriate for Ashok to adopt and why?
(e) What type of training would you suggest for police officers posted to such districts where stone mining illegal activities are rampant?

You have done an MBA from a reputed institution three years back but could not get campus placement due to COVID-19-generated recession. After competitive tests and interviews, you got a job in a leading shoe company. You have aged dependent parents and recently got married. You were allotted the Inspection Section responsible for clearing the final product.

A large consignment to Europe was rejected by the inspecting team for poor quality and returned. Top management ordered that the same consignment be cleared for the domestic market. You observed glaring poor quality and informed the Team Commander, but management told the team to overlook the defects. Other members signed and cleared the consignment. You warned that this would tarnish the company’s reputation, but management threatened termination if you refused to clear it.

(a) Under the given conditions, what are the options available to you as a member of the Inspecting Team?
(b) Critically evaluate each of the options listed by you.
(c) What option would you adopt and why?
(d) What are the ethical dilemmas being faced by you?
(e) What can be the consequences of overlooking the observations raised by the Inspecting Team?

Rakesh was working as Joint Commissioner in the Transport Department of a city and was entrusted with overseeing the control and functioning of the City Transport Department. A strike by the drivers’ union arose over compensation to a driver who died on duty while driving Bus No. 528.

The deceased driver had an altercation with a middle-aged car driver after an accident. The quarrel escalated into physical violence, both were injured and the bus driver later died. Police investigation found that the bus driver had started the quarrel and resorted to physical violence. The City Transport Department was considering not giving extra compensation. The deceased was 52, the sole earner, survived by his wife and two school/college-going daughters. The union demanded full extra compensation as given to other drivers who died on duty and employment for one family member; the strike continued for 10 days.

(a) What are the options available to Rakesh to meet the above situation?
(b) Critically examine each of the options identified by Rakesh.
(c) What are the ethical dilemmas being faced by Rakesh?
(d) What course of action would Rakesh adopt to diffuse the above situation?

You are appointed as an officer heading the section in an Environment Pollution Control Board to ensure compliance and follow-up. A large number of small and medium industries in the region have environmental clearance and provide employment to many migrant workers. However, most remain polluting units causing air, water and soil pollution and persistent health problems for local people. It was confirmed that the majority were violating environmental compliance.

You issued notices requiring fresh environmental clearance, but faced hostility from industries, vested interests, local politicians and workers who feared unemployment. Industry owners requested that harsh action not be initiated because closures would cause financial losses, product shortages and suffering to labourers and consumers. Labour unions opposed closure. You also received threats. Colleagues advised you to act freely, while local NGOs demanded immediate closure of polluting units.

(a) What are the options available to you under the given situation?
(b) Critically examine the options listed by you.
(c) What type of mechanism would you suggest to ensure environmental compliance?
(d) What are the ethical dilemmas you faced in exercising your option?
